entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Coirpre Cromm mac Crimthainn, who died in 577 CE, was a pivotal figure in the early medieval political landscape of Ireland, serving as King of Munster from approximately 546 to 577 CE. As a prominent member of the powerful Eóganachta dynasty, his reign represents a crucial phase in the consolidation of their authority over the southwestern province, laying foundational structures for what would become one of Ireland's most enduring and influential royal houses. His period of rule, though situated in the "Classical Era" as per the entity definition, firmly belongs to the post-Roman, pre-Viking age of Gaelic Ireland, characterized by nascent kingdoms and evolving legal systems.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Coirpre Cromm mac Crimthainn was instrumental in establishing the Eóganachta dynasty's long-term dominance in Munster, a political achievement that profoundly shaped the region's history for over five centuries. His reign marks a critical phase in the transition from tribal confederations to more structured kingdoms in Early Medieval Ireland.
